why: The repo is supposed to get smarter, which needs a memory with the same spine as the candidate shelf: a lesson is a claim, a claim cites evidence, and evidence has to open. Version 2 added the two charter-section-5 gates that made the memory honest rather than merely readable: a plane field so a lesson is typed by kind (issue #25) and a measured, enforced contradiction rule so no two active lessons can disagree silently (issue #24). Version 3 adds the validity window (phase 44): an optional verified_at and expires, so a claim whose window has passed is a named gate row instead of a silent certainty. scripts/memory.py reads every key below; nothing here is decorative.

id.means: mem-<slug>, unique in the ledger. Reusing a label conflates two lessons.

date.means: ISO 8601 UTC. Memory that cannot be ordered cannot be aged or superseded.

cue.means: the situation the lesson applies to, phrased so a different agent can recognise it before it acts.

lesson.means: what to do next time, as an instruction another agent could follow.

evidence.means: paths in this repo, URLs, or probe ids. An entry that does not resolve is a fabricated memory and the gate refuses the row.

confidence.means: how much this lesson is trusted. Retrieval orders by it; an unweighted lesson would be believed exactly as much as a measured one.

verdict.means: what the measurement said, same vocabulary as rules/candidate.schema.json. proposed means written down but not yet confirmed by a run.

plane.means: which memory plane the lesson is about: one of the eight ids declared in 15_SYSTEM/config/system.json -> memory_planes (project, repository, agent, task, error, decision, knowledge, conversation), or the stated value 'unclassified' when the row's source and topics do not decide. This is issue #25: before the field existed the map's claim that the error plane holds lessons was honest-but-weak, because a lesson from a failed run looked identical to a lesson from a design choice until you read the prose. The vocabulary is read from the config, never retyped here -- there is no second taxonomy.

topics.means: retrieval handles; --recall reads them, and the contradiction rule (issue #24) treats a shared topic as one of the four conditions.

source.means: where the lesson came from (a chat, an issue, a commit). A provenance line, not evidence. --migrate-planes and the --add default read it to decide a plane.

supersedes.means: the id of the lesson this one retires. Superseded rows stay in the ledger for the record and drop out of MEMORY.md's active table. A pair that contradicts but is linked by supersedes is reported as resolved, not refused (issue #24).

verified_at.means: the calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) a person last re-checked this row's evidence. It is a statement about the check, not about the claim: an absent field means nobody re-checked it, and the gate never invents a day. A value in the future, or one after `expires`, is invalid and refused -- a window that closed before it opened is a typo, and a verification that has not happened yet is a fabrication.

expires.means: the last calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on which this claim still counts as certain. Absent means EVERGREEN: the row states no window, so nothing can pass. Present and today or later means current. Present and in the past means STALE, which is a named gate row: --check refuses it, --windows counts it, --recall marks it, and MEMORY.md keeps the line. The gate never deletes, rewrites or hides a stale row -- retiring a claim is a human act through --add --supersedes, and re-verifying it is a human act through --verified-at/--expires on a new row.

validity_window.status: shipped and enforced (phase 44); Graphiti's bi-temporal edge reduced to two date fields, with no LLM in the write path
validity_window.rule: no expires = evergreen | expires >= today = current | expires < today = stale | unreadable or impossible window = invalid. Compared on calendar days, in the reader's today, with the repo's own date.today(); no timezone arithmetic a clone could disagree about.
validity_window.why_stale_is_refused: A claim whose window has passed may still be true -- but a reader holding only this clone cannot re-check it, and reporting it as merely OK is how a memory starts certifying what it can no longer open. The refusal names the row, the days past, and the two human acts that resolve it (re-verify, or supersede).
validity_window.measured_on_the_shipped_ledger: 2026-11-02, `python scripts/memory.py --windows`: 27 row(s), 27 evergreen, 0 current, 0 stale, 0 invalid. Not one shipped row carries either field, so the default had to be `absent = evergreen` -- a rule keyed on the existing `date` field would have called rows aged, which is a different claim than an expired window, and the honest answer to 'how many are stale under your rule' is zero because no row stated a window to pass. No date was written into lessons.jsonl to make the gate bite.
validity_window.enforced_by: python scripts/memory.py --check (invalid window per row, stale as a named refusal) and --windows (the report with its numbers); --add refuses a broken window before the write; --recall marks a stale answer instead of hiding it. The machine plane's reader obeys the same rule: mcp_server.py's memory_recall tool calls memory.recall() and appends memory.recall_mark(), so an agent sees the identical STALE suffix and the row is still returned.

contradiction.definition: two ACTIVE lessons contradict when all four hold on folded text: same plane, at least one shared topic, cue-overlap Jaccard >= 0.50, opposite verdict (helped vs hurt). Jaccard is |intersection|/|union| over the token sets the repo's own tokens() produces (lowercased, stopwords and short words dropped) -- stdlib, reproducible from a clone, no model, no embedding.
contradiction.threshold_evidence: measured on the shipped ledger (325 active pairs): the closest same-plane, shared-topic pair scores 0.31 and AGREES, and 0 pairs of opposite verdict exist at any threshold -- so 0.50 fires only on cues that describe the same situation in opposing terms, never on shared vocabulary. Because the shipped ledger holds no contradiction, none was rewritten; the rule is proven with fixtures.
contradiction.enforced_by: python scripts/memory.py --check refuses an active conflict; --contradictions reports every pair with its numbers and treats a supersedes-linked pair as resolved.

invariants: one row per id; a duplicate label is refused
every evidence entry resolves on disk, as a URL, or as a probe id
every row carries a plane in the mapped vocabulary (or the stated 'unclassified'); an unlabelled lesson is refused by --add and by --check (issue #25)
no two ACTIVE lessons may contradict -- same plane + shared topic + cue-overlap Jaccard >= 0.50 + opposite verdict is a refusal, not a cleanup task (issue #24)

a window field is either absent or a YYYY-MM-DD day that is not in the future and does not close before it opens; --add refuses it before the write and --check refuses the row that arrived by hand (phase 44)

a stale lesson is reported, never edited: --check names 'STALE <id>' and the ledger bytes, MEMORY.md's line and the row's own history survive the refusal -- deleting a stale claim to go green replaces one lie with a quieter one (phase 44)
MEMORY.md is a rendering: every active row appears in it and every mem-* id in it exists in the ledger
supersedes points at a row the ledger actually holds
the ledger is append-only -- a lesson is retired by superseding it, never by deleting the line
empty_is_legal: --recall with no hits prints NO_ENTRY and exits 0. Saying 'nothing in memory applied' is data; inventing a lesson to fill the silence is how the memory starts lying. The same rule reads the other way: an absent window is a stated absence, so it is evergreen -- not stale, and not a date to be filled in.
enforced_by: python scripts/memory.py --check (plane field, contradiction rule, validity windows), wired into scripts/health.py; python scripts/memory.py --contradictions reports the numbers behind each judgement; python scripts/memory.py --windows reports the state of every dated claim
